EMERGENCY NOTE   Date: 2026-05-28
42M, emergency department visit for a medication bridge supply.

S:
Patient presents to the emergency department because his pharmacy cannot fill his transplant medications until next week, and he has two days of tablets left. He wants to avoid any gap in his regimen. He feels well today and has taken every dose on schedule. He uses his rescue inhaler about once a week, mostly after dust exposure at work, and has not needed it more often this spring. He checks his blood pressure at home and reports readings in the low 120s. Patient denies depression. He works as a warehouse forklift operator and wears a dust mask on most shifts. Sister with schizophrenia. Father with heart failure. Lives with his spouse. Never smoker, rare alcohol.

O:
BP 126/80, HR 76, RR 14, Temp 98.4 F, SpO2 98% on room air.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: oropharynx clear.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally, good air movement.
Abdomen: soft, nontender, well-healed transplant incision in the right lower quadrant.
Extremities: warm and well perfused.
Labs (today): basic metabolic panel within normal limits, creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, eGFR stable post-transplant, tacrolimus trough sent.

A/P:
1. History of chronic kidney disease stage 4, resolved after kidney transplant. Graft function stable by today's labs. Provided a 3-day bridge supply of his current immunosuppressants at the same doses. Transplant team paged and agrees with the plan; the trough result will be routed to them.
2. Asthma, uncomplicated, using inhaler as needed. Lungs clear today. Albuterol refill provided. Continue dust mask use at work.
3. Essential hypertension, well controlled on current regimen. Continue current antihypertensive at the same dose.
4. Family history: reviewed father's cardiac history; no change to today's plan.

Discharged home in stable condition. Pick up regular prescriptions next week and keep the next transplant clinic visit as scheduled.
